outline.chapter_title: Motivation and Challenges of Long Context in LLMs
outline.description: Introduces why extending the context window is important, outlines practical scenarios that require millions of tokens, and reviews the fundamental obstacles faced by existing methods.
subtopics: Limitations of standard LLM context windows (e.g., LLaMA2 4k)
Applications that benefit from ultra‑long context (in‑context learning, agents, retrieval‑augmented generation)
Existing extensions up to ~128k and their shortcomings
Three core challenges: catastrophic new positions, scarcity of ultra‑long training data, and degradation of short‑context performance

outline.description: Covers the theory and implementation of Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE), the mathematical foundations of positional interpolation, and a survey of prior interpolation techniques.
subtopics: Formal definition of RoPE and its frequency‑based dimensions
Extension ratio and unified formulation of positional interpolation
Linear Position Interpolation (PI)
Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK)‑based interpolation & extrapolation
YaRN: frequency‑grouped interpolation
Limitations of uniform and hand‑crafted approaches

outline.chapter_title: Empirical Analysis of Non‑Uniform Positional Interpolation
outline.description: Presents the experimental findings that reveal two crucial non‑uniformities—across RoPE dimensions and across token positions—and demonstrates their impact on perplexity without fine‑tuning.
subtopics: Design of the evolutionary search for optimal per‑dimension scaling
Finding 1: dimension‑wise non‑uniformity improves 8× extension without fine‑tuning
Finding 2: preserving early token positions reduces interpolation loss
Finding 3: non‑uniform interpolation benefits both fine‑tuned and non‑fine‑tuned regimes
Summary of insights and their implications for extension strategies

outline.description: Formalizes the search problem, defines the rescaling function, and introduces the two control variables (per‑dimension λ and early‑token threshold ĥn).
subtopics: Mathematical expression of RoPE with non‑uniform rescale factors
Objective: minimizing next‑token loss (perplexity) on ultra‑long sequences
Constraints and design choices (monotonicity, search space limits)
Discussion of why this is a combinatorial optimization problem

outline.description: Details the efficient evolutionary algorithm, including population initialization, mutation, crossover, and the monotonicity constraint that drastically reduces search cost.
subtopics: Search space definition (λ range, ĥn candidates)
Population seeding with PI, NTK, and YaRN baselines
Mutation and crossover operators under monotonic λ constraint
Evaluation metric (perplexity on a small validation set)
Algorithm pseudo‑code and computational considerations

outline.chapter_title: Progressive Extension Strategy to 2 Million Tokens
outline.description: Explains the three‑stage pipeline—initial large‑ratio interpolation, lightweight fine‑tuning at 256 k, and a second interpolation—to reach 2048 k tokens with only ~1 k fine‑tuning steps.
subtopics: Stage 1: Non‑uniform interpolation to 128 k and 256 k (no fine‑tuning)
Stage 2: Fine‑tuning the model at 256 k (400 steps + 600 steps)
Stage 3: Second search on the fine‑tuned model to reach 2048 k
Why progressive extension is more efficient than direct 2048 k fine‑tuning
Handling of GPU and data constraints

outline.description: Describes how to mitigate the performance drop on the original 4 k–8 k windows after massive extension by re‑searching λ for short lengths and dynamically switching RoPE at inference.
subtopics: Analysis of position crowding after 512× extension
Secondary evolution search for 4 k/8 k windows
Dynamic RoPE selection during inference based on sequence length
Impact on benchmark performance

outline.description: Presents a comprehensive set of experiments that validate LongRoPE on LLaMA2‑7B and Mistral‑7B across perplexity, retrieval, and standard benchmarks.
subtopics: Setup: datasets, fine‑tuning hyper‑parameters, evaluation metrics
Perplexity results on Proof‑pile and PG‑19 up to 256 k
Perplexity on Books3 beyond 2 M tokens
Passkey retrieval task and analysis of effective context length
Zero‑shot/Few‑shot performance on ARC‑Challenge, HellaSwag, MMLU, TruthfulQA
Comparison with state‑of‑the‑art baselines (PI, NTK, YaRN, LongLoRA, etc.)

outline.description: Investigates the contribution of each component of LongRoPE through controlled experiments.
subtopics: Effect of the second positional interpolation after fine‑tuning
Impact of short‑context recovery on 4 k/8 k perplexity and benchmark scores
Separate ablation of dimension‑wise vs. token‑position non‑uniformities
Sensitivity to population size, mutation rate, and monotonicity constraint

outline.description: Situates LongRoPE within the broader landscape of long‑context techniques, including retrieval‑augmented models, attention‑mask innovations, and other fine‑tuning‑based extensions.
subtopics: Retrieval‑based and memory‑augmented LLMs
Attention‑mask and sparse‑attention approaches
Fine‑tuning methods that scale RoPE base or use LoRA
How LongRoPE complements or improves upon these methods

outline.description: Provides a step‑by‑step recipe for practitioners to apply LongRoPE to any RoPE‑based LLM, including code snippets, resource estimates, and troubleshooting tips.
subtopics: Preparing the search dataset (short validation samples)
Running the evolutionary search (parameters, hardware)
Fine‑tuning schedule for 128 k / 256 k windows
Integrating dynamic RoPE selection into inference pipelines
Release information (GitHub repository, model checkpoints)

outline.description: Discusses potential extensions, such as applying LongRoPE to other positional schemes, scaling to even larger windows, and combining with attention‑mask methods.
subtopics: Adapting the search to ALiBi, T5‑relative, etc.
Joint optimization of RoPE and attention patterns
Reducing the need for any fine‑tuning
Evaluation on downstream tasks (summarization, code generation)
Ethical considerations of ultra‑long context models
